key_insight: SAGE-PINN embeds axisymmetric cylindrical geometry and conservation laws into the network so the singular axis terms disappear by construction, enabling stable PINN training for coupled flow and heat transfer.
engineering_relevance: It offers a mesh-free way to simulate stenosed-artery nanofluid flow and thermal transport in cylindrical coordinates without case-specific tuning, which is useful for biomedical and multiphysics design studies.
method: Uses the parity-preserving variable s = r^2 and a modified stream-function form to remove explicit 1/r singularities.
Enforces boundary conditions exactly with analytical ansätze and trains in staged momentum-thermal-joint phases.
Adds residual normalization, continuation in Péclet/Richardson numbers, and a physics-scaled drift guard for optimization stability.
evidence_signal: Validated against finite-element reference solutions; reported mass conservation at single-precision round-off and central-range errors of 1.6% for axial velocity and 9.1% for temperature.
watch_item: Accuracy degrades in strongly buoyancy-influenced slow-flow regimes and in highly advection-dominated heat-transfer cases, so those extremes may need extra stabilization or tuning.
paper_title: SAGE-PINN: A Singularity-free Axisymmetric Geometry-Encoded Physics-Informed Neural Network for Axisymmetric Multiphysics Flow in Cylindrical Coordinates
